messages.subject: Solar time
parts:
Hi all, 

It's intuitive to convert from clock time to solar time when assessing diel activity. 
There are a few r packages to do this (e.g. The solaR R package by Oscar Perpiñán Lamigueiro), but I was wandering, before I dive into this, if anyone had some code (that they would be willing to share) to directly convert a camtrapr record table to solar time? Or even recommendations about the best way to go about this?

Cheers,
Matt.

messages.subject: Re: Solar time
parts:
Matt

We have done a lot of work here but ...  As an exercise we are replicating Ikeda et al's paper. I am just discussing with my brother (my R guru) what we did and why.

My thinking is -
assign the time zone to GTM+10 (or -10 - I get muddled and have to check).  That solves the discontinuity with Australia daylight saving.
we have done the analysis of diel activity on this time zone.
for every record my brother calculated dawn and dusk (with an R package) and arbitrarily defined 
       dawn twilight plus-minus 1 hour of sunrise
       dusk twilight plus-minus 1 hour of sunset
my brother plotted a ggplot version of the diel activity (with confidence intervals)
       there is some discussion to be had on how we test for difference
(we also looked at what was an independent record).

We are open to discussion or correction but my first thought is that adjusting for difference in sunrise-sunset across a 600  Squ km study area is overkill. If you did that you might need to correct for topography - especially in the Otway Ranges but unnecessary for Western Port 'plains'.  Using solar time for each location of each image and differentiating between - for example noon (mid way between dawn and dusk) verses the time of the sun's highest point in the sky might again be overkill.

These are my musings.

I'd welcome help finding reviews or references defining and applying definitions of crepuscular, cathermeral to real mammals.  I don't have easy access to the literature.
regards
David
